## Required

| Variable | What it is | Values | Default | When to set it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTH_SECRET` | Signs your login-session cookie. | 64 hex characters | _required_ | Always, on every deployment. Generate it with `openssl rand -hex 32` — never reuse one between instances. | No default. Boot fails if it is shorter than 32 characters. Changing it invalidates every existing session, so you are signed out. |
| `WEB_ORIGIN` | Comma-separated list of exact browser origins allowed for CORS, login CSRF, and the WebSocket upgrade. | comma-separated origins, no wildcards | _required_ | Always. Set it to the address you open the app at, e.g. `https://bot.example.com`. List several, comma-separated, to serve the SPA on more than one origin. | No default. Boot fails if it is empty or if any entry contains `*` — credentialed CORS forbids a wildcard, and allowing one would loosen the auth gate only. A mismatch shows as a browser that loads the page but cannot sign in. |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Postgres connection string, read by every process. | a Postgres connection string | _required_ | Always, unless you use the bundled Compose Postgres — the compose files supply an in-network default. | No default. Boot crashes if unset rather than silently connecting to `localhost`, which is the failure a fallback would hide. |
| `REDIS_URL` | Redis connection string for the job queues and caches. | a Redis connection string | _required_ | Always, unless you use the bundled Compose Redis. Include the password when Redis requires auth: `redis://:pw@host:6379`. | No default. Boot crashes if unset, for the same reason as the database URL. |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | Password the bundled Postgres container initialises with. | any string | `postgres` — the production overlay uses a secret file instead | On any Compose deployment. Change it from the shipped value before exposing the stack to anything. | `.env.example` ships `postgres`. The production overlay reads a `deploy/secrets/*` file instead and ignores this variable. Changing it after first boot does NOT change the existing database password — the container only initialises once. |

## Runtime

| Variable | What it is | Values | Default | When to set it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_ENV` | Selects development or production framework behaviour. | `development`, `test`, `production` | `development` | Rarely — the container image sets it. Set it to `production` if you run the app outside the image. | Development mode adds verbose framework output and disables some caching. |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | Log verbosity for the worker, the loudest process in the stack. | `fatal`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace` | `info` | While debugging. Turn it back down afterwards. | `debug` and `trace` flood stdout and can fill a disk on a busy account. `warn` and above will hide the routine decision log you usually want. |
| `ROLE` | Which listeners and consumers this process runs. | `all`, `api`, `worker`, `study` | `all` | Only when splitting the stack across containers. The single-box default runs everything in one process. | `all` runs the api, the live worker and the backtest consumer on one event loop, which is why the tuning defaults below are conservative. Splitting into `api` + `worker` + `study` keeps a long backtest off the trading loop. Only the `api` role runs database migrations. |
| `LIVE_DEMO` | Turns the instance into a public, no-login sandbox. | `1` or `true` to enable; anything else is off | `off` — the flag parses to a boolean, so the schema default is `false` | Only on a throwaway public demo box. Never on an instance holding your keys. | Injects a demo operator for every anonymous request; blocks credential, notifier, backup/restore, account-creation, account-rename/delete, retention-change, diagnosis-start, fee-reconciliation, and archive-backfill routes; suppresses all notifier sending; and refuses to boot if any account is on live Binance. Trading remains interactive on Binance testnet. Only `1` or `true` enable it. |
| `MCP_ENABLED` | Mounts the authenticated MCP control plane an AI agent drives the bot through. | `1` or `true` to enable; anything else is off | `off` — the flag parses to a boolean, so the schema default is `false` | Only when you want Claude Code or ChatGPT to read and trade this instance. It is a public, internet-reachable trading surface, so leave it off until you have read the MCP architecture doc. | Off, no `/api/mcp` route is mounted at all and no protected-resource metadata is published, so there is no agent surface to secure rather than a guarded one to trust. On, the route is mounted behind OAuth 2.1 bearer authorization and requires `MCP_RESOURCE_URL`. It is refused outright while `LIVE_DEMO` is on, because that mode injects the operator id for anonymous callers. |
| `MCP_RESOURCE_URL` | Canonical resource identifier agents bind their access tokens to, normally `https://<your-host>/api/mcp`. | an absolute `https` URL with no query string, fragment or embedded credentials, no trailing slash | _required_ — optional while `MCP_ENABLED` is off; required when it is on | Whenever `MCP_ENABLED` is true. | Must be the URL an agent actually reaches, not an internal or container address: tokens are audience-bound to this exact string, so a value that disagrees with the public hostname produces a 401 that explains nothing. A trailing slash is trimmed automatically. `https` is required because this value is also the auth base URL, so the issuer, the JWKS document and every authorization endpoint follow it; plain `http` is accepted only when the host is loopback (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `[::1]`), where the bytes never leave the machine, which is what local development uses. Boot fails if it is missing while `MCP_ENABLED` is true, if it is not a valid URL, if it is plaintext `http` on a non-loopback host, or if it carries a query string, a fragment or userinfo. |
| `PUBLIC_WEB_URL` | Base URL used to build tap-through links inside operator notifications. | an absolute URL, no trailing slash | _required_ — optional: unset means notifications send without a link | When you want a Slack or Telegram alert to link straight to the relevant screen. | Optional. Unset, notifications still send — just without a link. A trailing slash is trimmed automatically. Boot fails if the value is not a valid URL. |

## Sign-in

| Variable | What it is | Values | Default | When to set it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PASSWORD_SIGN_IN_ENABLED` | Whether the sign-in page offers the email and password form. | `1`, `true`, `0` or `false`; any other value fails boot | `on` — the flag parses to a boolean, so the schema default is `true` | Turn it off once single sign-on works and you want the identity provider, and the multi-factor authentication you turned on there, to be the only way in. | Off, the form is hidden and the password sign-in and sign-up endpoints answer 404. A mistyped value fails boot rather than silently turning the form off. At least one of this and `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ENABLED` must be on. If single sign-on then cannot be reached at boot and no other method works, password sign-in is switched back on for that run and a security alert is sent, so the instance is never left with no way in. The `reset-password` command works either way. |
| `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ENABLED` | Offers "sign in with single sign-on" through an OpenID Connect identity provider such as Auth0. | `1` or `true` to enable; anything else is off | `off` — the flag parses to a boolean, so the schema default is `false` | When you want your identity provider (and its multi-factor authentication) to guard sign-in. | On, it requires `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ISSUER_URL`, `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_CLIENT_ID`, `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_CLIENT_SECRET` and `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, and it is refused together with `LIVE_DEMO`. The provider is checked at boot with a 5-second limit; if it cannot be reached the app still starts with the button disabled, raises a security alert, and exits once the provider answers again so it restarts with the provider registered. That restart depends on the container restart policy (`restart: unless-stopped` in the prod and scale compose files); with no policy the api stays stopped. Only the identity that created the operator, or one linked later from Settings > Security, can sign in; nobody else can create an account through it. |
| `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ISSUER_URL` | The identity provider's issuer, for example `https://your-tenant.auth0.com/`. | an absolute `https` URL, written exactly as the provider publishes it | _required_ — optional while `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ENABLED` is off; required when it is on | Whenever `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ENABLED` is on. | It is compared character for character with the `issuer` in the provider's discovery document and with every ID token, so keep the trailing slash Auth0 uses. A mismatch disables single sign-on at boot. Plain `http` is accepted only for a loopback host. |
| `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_CLIENT_ID` | Identifies this app to the identity provider. | the client ID of the application you created at the provider | _required_ — optional while `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ENABLED` is off; required when it is on | Whenever `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ENABLED` is on. | A wrong value makes the provider refuse the sign-in; the app records the failure and the sign-in page shows a plain error. |
| `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_CLIENT_SECRET` | Proves to the identity provider that sign-in requests really come from this app. | the client secret of the application you created at the provider | _required_ — optional while `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ENABLED` is off; required when it is on | Whenever `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ENABLED` is on. | Kept in the environment only, never in the database, so a stolen session cannot read or change it. Rotating it at the provider needs a restart with the new value. |
| `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_BUTTON_LABEL` | The text on the single sign-on button, for example `Sign in with Auth0`. | 1 to 40 characters | `Single sign-on` | When you want the button to name your provider. | Shown only when single sign-on is enabled. Boot fails if it is empty or longer than 40 characters. |
| `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | The address you reach this app at, as the browser sees it. | an origin only, for example `https://bot.example.com`: scheme, host and optional port, no path | _required_ — optional while `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ENABLED` is off; required when it is on | Whenever `SINGLE_SIGN_ON_ENABLED` is on. Register `<PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/api/auth/callback/oidc` as the callback URL at the provider. | The single sign-on callback address is built from it, never from request headers, so a proxy or a forged `Host` header cannot redirect a sign-in elsewhere. Must be `https` except on a loopback host, and must share its origin with `MCP_RESOURCE_URL` when both are set. |

## HTTP and admin ports

| Variable | What it is | Values | Default | When to set it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | Port serving the API and the single-page app. | a port number | `3000` | If 3000 is already taken on the host. | Must differ from the admin port, or boot fails with a clear message rather than a port-in-use crash. |
| `ADMIN_PORT` | Port for the api's health and metrics endpoints. | a port number | `9100` | If 9100 is taken. Kept separate from the public port so a slow scrape cannot starve it. | Serves `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics`, all unauthenticated. |
| `ADMIN_HOST` | Interface the api's admin server binds. | an interface address | `127.0.0.1` | On Kubernetes, set it to `0.0.0.0` so the kubelet probes reach the pod IP. | The default binds loopback only, keeping the unauthenticated admin endpoints off the LAN. If you open it up, restrict the port with a NetworkPolicy — a Service is not a firewall. |
| `WORKER_ADMIN_PORT` | Port for the worker's health and metrics endpoints. | a port number | `9101` | If 9101 is taken on the host. | Defaults to one above the api's so both can run on one host during development. Inside Compose each container has its own loopback, so they could share a port. |
| `WORKER_ADMIN_HOST` | Interface the worker's admin server binds. | an interface address | `127.0.0.1` | On Kubernetes, for the same probe reason as the api. | Loopback by default; the same NetworkPolicy caveat applies if you widen it. |
| `APP_HTTP_PORT` | Host port the app publishes on under Docker Compose. | a host port number | `80` — unset, the base and scale compose files publish on 3000 and the production file on 80 | To publish on a port other than the compose default, e.g. behind a reverse proxy on 8080. | Compose-only; the application never reads it. Unset, the base and scale compose files publish on 3000 and the production file on 80. |

## Database

| Variable | What it is | Values | Default | When to set it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POSTGRES_DB` | Database name the bundled Postgres creates on first boot. | a Postgres identifier | `binance_trading_bot` — compose-only | Rarely. Change it only before the first boot — it has no effect afterwards. | Compose-only. The application reads the database name out of the connection string, not from here, so changing one without the other breaks the connection. |
| `POSTGRES_USER` | Superuser the bundled Postgres creates on first boot. | a Postgres identifier | `postgres` — compose-only | Rarely, and only before first boot. | Compose-only, and subject to the same first-boot-only caveat as the database name. |
| `PGSSLMODE` | libpq SSL mode used by the backup and restore commands. | `disable`, `allow`, `prefer`, `require`, `verify-ca`, `verify-full` | `prefer` | When Postgres is behind TLS and you want backups to require or verify it. | Applies to `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` only — the app's own driver has its own SSL configuration and ignores this. `.env.example` ships `disable` for a local plaintext Postgres. |
| `API_DB_POOL_MAX` | Maximum Postgres connections the api process opens. | a positive integer | `10` — hard-coded in `packages/db/src/pool.ts`; no zod schema parses it | When Postgres reports too many clients, or when the api queues behind its own pool under load. | Read straight off the environment, and only a plain run of digits is accepted: `10.5`, `1e3` and `+5` all fail pool creation outright, while an empty or whitespace-only value falls back to the default. Every replica opens up to this many connections, so the server-side limit is this times the replica count. Exhausting the pool no longer hangs: a checkout that waits longer than the 5s deadline in `packages/db/src/pool.ts` fails, and the request answers 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with a `db_pool_checkout_timeout` warn line naming the path — so raising this value is a response to those 503s, not to a silent stall. Raise it only for that log name. Its sibling `db_connect_timeout` is the same 5s deadline expiring on a new connection the database never finished accepting, which means the pool had room and more connections would only aim more concurrent attempts at a server already failing to answer. |
| `WORKER_DB_POOL_MAX` | Maximum Postgres connections the worker process opens. | a positive integer | `25` — hard-coded in `packages/db/src/pool.ts`; no zod schema parses it | For the same reasons as the api pool. The worker default is larger because tick jobs run concurrently. | Sized against `TICK_CONCURRENCY`: set it below that and ticks serialise on connection checkout rather than on the concurrency limit you configured. Read straight off the environment, and only a plain run of digits is accepted: `10.5`, `1e3` and `+5` all fail pool creation outright, while an empty or whitespace-only value falls back to the default. |
| `ADMIN_DB_POOL_MAX` | Maximum Postgres connections the migration and maintenance pool opens. | a positive integer | `2` — hard-coded in `packages/db/src/pool.ts`; no zod schema parses it | Almost never. This pool runs migrations and admin tasks, which are serial by nature. | Deliberately tiny so a maintenance task cannot starve the trading pools. Raising it buys nothing, because nothing here runs in parallel. Read straight off the environment, and only a plain run of digits is accepted: `10.5`, `1e3` and `+5` all fail pool creation outright, while an empty or whitespace-only value falls back to the default. |

## Retention (days before pruning)

| Variable | What it is | Values | Default | When to set it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DISCOVERY_SNAPSHOT_RETENTION_DAYS` | How long auto-discovery universe snapshots are kept. | a positive integer | `180` | Raise it before running a discovery net-edge backtest, which needs a long series. | Deliberately generous, because this series is meant to accumulate. A short horizon defeats its purpose and cannot be backfilled. |
| `EQUITY_SNAPSHOT_RETENTION_DAYS` | How long the per-profile equity series behind the profit-vs-hold chart is kept. | a positive integer | `365` | Raise it to keep a multi-year equity curve. | Roughly 96 rows per profile per day, so the storage cost is modest. Trimming it shortens the chart permanently. |

## Worker tuning

| Variable | What it is | Values | Default | When to set it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BACKTEST_CONCURRENCY` | How many backtest replays may run at once. | a positive integer | `1` | Raise it on a dedicated backtest box; keep it at 1–2 when the worker shares a core with live trading. | Replays are CPU-bound, so raising this on a shared box adds tail latency to the dashboard and the trading loop. `.env.example` ships `4` for a dedicated study box. |
| `STUDY_CPU_SHARE` | Fraction of one core a backtest replay may consume. | a number in (0, 1] | _required_ — resolved at boot: `0.5` under `ROLE=all`, else `1.0` | To trade backtest speed against live responsiveness when both share a process. | Unset resolves to 0.5 under `ROLE=all` and 1.0 for a dedicated worker or study process, so the default already does the right thing. The runner sleeps at yield points to hold the share, so a low value makes backtests proportionally slower. |
| `TICK_CONCURRENCY` | How many per-symbol tick jobs may run at once. | a positive integer | `25` | Lower it if the dashboard feels sluggish while many symbols are active under `ROLE=all`. | Ordering per (profile, symbol) is enforced regardless of this value, so lowering it only reduces throughput — never correctness. |
| `KLINE_CONCURRENCY` | How many Binance candle fetches the technicals job runs at once per interval. | a positive integer | `8` | Lower it if technical-rating computation is monopolising the event loop, or to reduce burst request weight. | Each fetched symbol then runs synchronous indicator maths, so this bounds how many bursts stack up. |
| `TICK_PERSIST_TIMEOUT_MS` | Time budget for the durable per-tick strategy-state write. | a positive integer, milliseconds | `100` | Raise it on network-replicated storage, where a commit is a cross-node round trip. | On timeout the tick falls back to a degraded cache path, which is safe but is meant to be rare. Left too low on slow storage, the fallback becomes the steady state. The default suits a local SSD. |
| `WORKER_FRAME_TRACE` | Records live tick inputs and decisions as JSONL for deterministic replay. | `1` to enable; anything else is off | `off` — read directly by the frame-recorder factory; unset is off | Only while diagnosing replay drift, then disable it and protect or delete the trace. | Each completed strategy tick appends balances, holdings, inputs, and decisions. The trace contains financial state and must not be committed. |
| `WORKER_FRAME_TRACE_FILE` | Output path for the optional worker frame trace. | a writable file path | `worker-frame-trace.jsonl under the OS temp directory` — resolved at runtime by `tmpdir()` when unset | When the default temporary path is unsuitable for a short diagnostic capture. | Used only when `WORKER_FRAME_TRACE=1`. Write failures are reported without stopping the trading tick. |
| `WORKER_REPLICAS` | Live-worker replica count in the scale compose file. | a positive integer | `1` — compose-only | Keep it at 1. Multi-replica scale-out is merged but dormant. | Compose interpolates it into the service replica count; application code never reads it. Raising it today runs untested concurrency paths. |

## Observability (OpenTelemetry)

| Variable | What it is | Values | Default | When to set it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | Service name stamped on exported traces. | any string | `binance-trading-bot` — compose-only | When you export traces and run more than one instance. | Ignored unless the OTLP endpoint below is set. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | OTLP collector endpoint. Setting it is what enables trace export. | a collector URL | _required_ — compose-only; empty disables the exporter | When you have a collector to send traces to. | Empty by default, so the exporter is off and no telemetry leaves the box. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` | Extra headers attached to the OTLP export request. | `key=value` pairs | _required_ — compose-only; empty by default | When your collector needs authentication. | Treat the value as a credential — it typically carries a token. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT` | Timeout for one OTLP trace export request. | milliseconds | `3000` — read directly by the OpenTelemetry bootstrap when export is enabled | Raise it only when a reachable collector routinely needs more than three seconds. | A timed-out export is counted as a dropped span batch. Trading work continues without waiting for telemetry. |
| `DEPLOY_ENV` | Deployment environment attached to exported traces. | an environment name such as `development`, `staging`, or `production` | `development` — read directly; unset falls back to `NODE_ENV`, then `development` | When the deployment name should differ from `NODE_ENV`. | `production` enables sampled tracing; other values keep the always-on development sampler unless code supplies an explicit environment. |

## Build and deploy

| Variable | What it is | Values | Default | When to set it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IMAGE_TAG` | Image tag Docker Compose pulls. | a Docker tag | `latest` — compose-only | To pin a release instead of tracking the moving latest tag. | The default moves with every release, so an unpinned deployment can change under you on the next pull. |
| `BACKUP_DIR` | Directory the scheduled backup writes dump files into. | an absolute path | `/backups` | To write backups somewhere other than the bundled volume. | The backup job creates the directory if missing, and the backup screen lists what is there. Point it outside the container volume and the dumps will not survive a container rebuild. |
| `GIT_SHA` | Build commit stamped into the image, surfaced on the status endpoint. | a git commit sha | `""` | Never by hand — the Docker build injects it. | Empty in a local build, where boot falls back to the local git commit or `unknown`. It is what lets the status bar spot api/worker version skew. |
| `WEB_DIST_DIR` | Directory of the built web app the api serves. | a directory path | `apps/web/dist` | Never by hand — the container image sets it. | If the directory is absent the api serves no web app at all, which is correct during development (Vite serves it) and for an api behind a CDN. |
